newsitem.title: BRAZIL: 22 dead in Amazon riverboat disaster.
newsitem.headline: 22 dead in Amazon riverboat disaster.

text.p: Twenty-two people died on Saturday when a riverboat with 80 people on board sank after hitting a log in a remote region of the Amazon, an official said.
Lt. Carlos Alberto Reis, of the Belem Firefighting Corps, said the riverboat went down in the middle of the night close to the town of Acara, 95 miles (150 kms) south of Belem.
He said the accident took place when most of the passengers were asleep and that several of those who died had been trapped underneath the deck.
"We are not entirely clear about the details because the place where the boat sank is six hours away by boat," Reis said in a telephone interview.
Port Authority officials sent divers to participate in the rescue operations and help retrieve the bodies that remained underneath the water.
Acara, a small town founded next to a river that has the same name, only has one phone, which was out of service on Saturday.
Riverboats are the preferred method of transport in the Amazon where the population takes advantage of a vast river network to move from one town to another.
